title: Elige el mundo visual de Cerquita
question: The roll assigned Cuadro de Mercado. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Cuadro de Mercado
options.lineage: Naïf canvases stacked at Mercado Modelo and on Calle El Conde
options.thesis: Each dog is shown like a market painting: one canvas at a time, in a painted frame, and you only take a few home.
materials: flat gouache color fields, no gradients
layered flat leaf silhouettes (plantain, palm, almendro)
options.viewport: One dog photo in a painted frame band filling about 70% of the screen. Leaves tuck behind the frame edges, the name and km are painted on the frame's lower band, the radius chip sits at the top, and two skip and save capsules sit within thumb reach.
options.risk: Leaves can tip into souvenir kitsch if overused. Market naïf is partly Haitian in origin, so it stays a shared Caribbean grammar of painted color with Dominican subjects.

raised.raise: One action color, used only on things you can tap. The frame colors never compete with the save button, which also fits the color study's finding about salience.
The dog's facts (age, size, energy, km) are a strip of labeled segments with tabular figures, not loose tags.
Moving the radius slider updates the dog count and distances in place, digit by digit, so you see what the change does.
The next dog is already loaded one gesture away, and photos fill their frame at any aspect ratio.

options.label: Ruta de Guagua
options.lineage: Hand-painted guagua and concho route placards, and the stripes on their bodywork
options.thesis: Distance is the route: each dog appears as a painted windshield placard announcing its name and how far it is.
options.viewport: A dog photo under a windshield-style placard reading 'LUNA · a 6 km · Los Mina'. The radius is a route stripe with stops, and actions sit on a bottom bumper bar.
options.risk: The transit metaphor may make adoption feel like logistics. It's very recognizable locally but could read loud for a careful decision.

options.label: Guide Map Lobes
options.lineage: Opening-day zoo and garden guide map
options.thesis: Your radius is a swelling lobe of flat color, with shelters pinned along its coast and each dog cropped into its own lobe.
options.viewport: A green lobe of 'your area' swells across the screen and the current dog's photo is cropped into it. A yellow capsule shows the km, and the controls are coral and blue capsules.
options.case: Fuses well and wins on product clarity, since the radius becomes the map. It loses on audience identification: it's a generic park map with nothing Dominican.
options.risk: Lobe crops can cut dogs awkwardly, and morphing SVG coastlines is costly on low-end phones.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards and one bright action color.
options.viewport: A stacked card column with a bottom bar.
options.case: Clear, but nobody recognizes it as theirs; it's indistinguishable from every pet app.
options.kept: The action color appears only where something can be tapped.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.thesis: A segmented pass and a live board.
options.viewport: The dog as a pass, with a board of nearby dogs.
options.case: Ranking by departure doesn't fit adoption, and the feel is cold and transactional.
options.kept: Facts shown as labeled segments with tabular figures.

options.label: Vertical Media Feed
options.thesis: One item fills the screen and the next is one flick away.
options.viewport: A full-screen dog with an action rail.
options.case: It is built for consumption, which contradicts 'consider, don't consume', and a black frame works against dark-coated dogs.
options.kept: Preloaded next item and photos that fit any aspect.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size, raked glass slides.
options.viewport: A raked rack of dog slides.
options.case: A raked lateral rack fights touch browsing and readability on a phone.
options.kept: Rank carried by weight and case, not a ladder of sizes.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Rows that flip character by character.
options.case: Dark and mechanical; it treats dogs as departures.
options.kept: Numbers that change animate in place, digit by digit.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A photo-first pet adoption app with swipe cards, done at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A stack of rounded photo cards, a heart and an X below, and tabs at the bottom.
canonCard.risk: It reads as 'Tinder for dogs', which is exactly what the product refuses to be.
